format: editorial-handoff-v1 (not a native HyperFrames import schema)
required_definition: Valkey is an open source (BSD) high-performance key/value datastore that supports a variety of workloads such as caching, message queues, and can act as a primary database. The project is backed by the Linux Foundation, ensuring it will remain open source forever.

scenes.title: Memory speed versus disk
scenes.narration: Memory access is faster than disk access. Valkey keeps working data in memory, with optional disk persistence.
scenes.direction: Open with two hardware-level paths from a processor: RAM and persistent disk/SSD. Animate the memory read arriving first, with no numeric latency, bar ratio, multiplier or benchmark axis. Label the comparison Conceptual. Then put Valkey around the in-memory working dataset with an optional persistence arrow to disk. Do not portray RAM as durable, networked Valkey as local RAM speed, or every database query as a physical disk read. End on the Valkey logo for the definition.

scenes.title: What Valkey is
scenes.narration: Valkey is an open source (BSD) high-performance key/value datastore that supports a variety of workloads such as caching, message queues, and can act as a primary database. The project is backed by the Linux Foundation, ensuring it will remain open source forever.
scenes.direction: Speak the exact requested definition over two phases relative to this scene: 0–12 seconds for the Valkey logo, key/value diagram and workloads; 12–19 seconds for Linux Foundation backing and OPEN SOURCE FOREVER. Attribute the commitment to valkey.io. Use phrase captions, not the entire paragraph on one frame.

scenes.title: SET a key and value
scenes.narration: Start with a key and a value. SET stores it. GET reads it back.
screen: START WITH A KEY AND VALUE
scenes.direction: Show an illustrative valkey-cli transcript, not a shell command. At scene-local 0–3s reveal SET Key Value; at 3s show OK. At 4–5s reveal GET Key, then show "Value" and hold. Keep Key and Value capitalization intact. No TTL is implied by this basic SET. The transcript is documented expected behavior, not a recorded execution.

scenes.title: Cache-aside: the everyday caching pattern
scenes.narration: Cache-aside is a common starting point. Your app checks Valkey first. On a miss, it reads the database and caches the result with an expiry. The next hit skips the database.
screen: Write path: update database, then invalidate cache
scenes.direction: Give caching the featured-use-case position requested by the employee, without inventing adoption percentages or a measured most-common ranking. Show the application owning each arrow. For the first read: app → Valkey GET product:42 → miss; app → primary database → product data; app → Valkey SET product:42 "blue mug" EX 60 → OK; app → caller returns product. For a second read while the entry is valid, app → Valkey → hit → caller, with no database arrow lit. Never draw Valkey fetching the database on a miss; that would imply read-through caching. A final small write-path note says update database, then invalidate cache. TTL and invalidation reduce staleness but do not guarantee consistency under races. Production needs failure and stampede handling.

scenes.title: Releases
scenes.narration: Choose stable releases, or explore the next release candidate.
scenes.direction: Show a compact static release board. Keep the preview in a separate outlined region with the word PREVIEW, never in the stable row. Numbers remain visual so narration does not rush. These are the stable releases featured on the homepage, not an exhaustive support matrix. Recheck just before render/publication.

scenes.title: Modules
scenes.narration: Extend Valkey with JSON, Search, Bloom, and LDAP modules.
scenes.direction: Attach four named extension tiles to the server. Display module names as text, not invented logos. The framing must show these as loadable modules. The Search tile covers full-text and vector search; Bloom is approximate membership, not a fraud classifier.

scenes.title: Integrations
scenes.narration: Connect through GLIDE, Spring Boot, Fastify, and Lambda Powertools.
scenes.direction: Show applications connecting through the client/integration layer. Ground the labels in spring-data-valkey, @fastify/valkey-glide, and the GLIDE-backed idempotency integrations for Powertools. These are distinct integrations, not one universal adapter. Use text labels to avoid adding unrequested third-party integration logos.

scenes.title: Use cases: application state and traffic
scenes.narration: Cache data, manage sessions, and control traffic.
scenes.direction: Reveal the five use-case labels together within 0.3 seconds, then hold. Use one request diagram with cache, session and traffic-control branches. Highlight existing labels rather than replacing them. Display a small Application patterns marker so this does not imply turnkey guarantees.

scenes.title: Use cases: service coordination
scenes.narration: Coordinate services and keep retries under control.
scenes.direction: Show a service-to-service request path with a lock, queued work and retry marker. Keep all five labels visible for almost the full scene. Do not suggest Pub/Sub persists chat history, distributed locks are failure-proof, or idempotency means exactly-once external effects.

scenes.title: Use cases: ordered data and membership
scenes.narration: Track rankings and event histories. Add Bloom filters for fraud-screening prechecks.
scenes.direction: Use a leaderboard and timestamped event stream. Add a Bloom membership gate feeding Verify against source, never Fraud detected. Pair Probabilistic membership with the smaller Fraud prechecks label, not a fifth independent capability. Streams is the event-log model; AOF persistence is documented separately in USE_CASES.md.

scenes.title: Use cases: documents, search and AI
scenes.narration: Build with JSON documents and full-text search. Add vector search, KV-cache offload, and semantic caching.
scenes.direction: Keep five large labels visible. Connect JSON documents to full-text and vector indexes. Show two distinct cache paths: inference tensor chunks for LLM KV cache offload, and similar prompts/answers for semantic cache. Embedding generation and inference live outside Valkey.

scenes.title: Semantic caching: vector similarity for AI
scenes.narration: For AI, embed the prompt and search cached vectors with Valkey Search. A close, valid match reuses the answer. Otherwise, call the model and cache the result. Check context and freshness before reuse.
screen: Close match + valid context + fresh answer?
Miss: call model → cache answer + embedding
scenes.direction: Use two non-sensitive illustrative prompts: What is the capital of France? and Capital city of France?, with cached answer Paris. A separate embedding model converts the second prompt into a vector. Show nearest neighbors within the correct scope in Valkey Search; animate a qualitative distance gate plus context/freshness checks, never a fabricated measured 98% match or a universal threshold. On a validated hit, return Paris and bypass response generation, not the embedding step. For a miss or failed validation, show the application invoking an external language model, storing prompt embedding and answer with expiry, and returning the answer. Keep both embedding and language models outside Valkey. A 2D point diagram is a conceptual projection, not the actual embedding dimensions. Do not reuse private answers across users or tenants.

scenes.title: Participant community
scenes.narration: Built together, by the Valkey community. Open source forever.
scenes.direction: Use all 21 non-Apple participant marks from PARTICIPANT_LOGOS.json in a balanced alphabetic 7-column by 3-row wall, fully visible within 0.3 seconds and held for the scene. Keep the Valkey logo and small valkey.io / GitHub labels above it; reserve the dominant quick-start CTA for the next scene. No scrolling carousel. Label Valkey project participants, not customers, sponsors or endorsements. Apple is excluded from all imagery, transitions and backgrounds.

scenes.title: Run Valkey: final command
scenes.narration: Run Valkey's core server with Docker using this command. Start building at valkey dot I O.
scenes.direction: Make the corrected Docker command the final hero. Reveal it by scene-local 1s, then keep the full command unchanged through the final frame. Use large monospace type. This is a shell command, unlike the earlier SET/GET CLI example. Do not add simulated startup logs or claim a successful live run. Caption Core server · Docker required so the audience does not infer the command installs Search, JSON or other modules. No published host port or persistent volume is configured by this minimal demo command. Do not portray it as a production deployment.
